bib.title: Scaling Neural Machine Translation
bib.venue: Proceedings of the Third Conference on Machine Translation (WMT), Volume 1: Research Papers

question: How far can reduced-precision arithmetic, very large batches and multi-machine synchronous training cut the training time of a big Transformer NMT model without losing accuracy?
hypothesis: Half-precision and large-batch training with a higher learning rate, then data parallelism across nodes, speed training substantially at unchanged accuracy.
contributions: FP16 training cuts training time by 65% with no effect on accuracy
Batches grown from 25k to over 400k tokens by gradient accumulation, with a higher learning rate, cut single-machine time a further 40%
Parallelising over 16 machines cuts time a further 90%; new state of the art on WMT'14 En-De and En-Fr
Scaling to filtered Paracrawl data improves En-De to 29.8 BLEU
Analysis of stragglers from variable sub-batch shapes

method.summary: A big Transformer in fairseq is trained on WMT En-De and En-Fr with mixed precision (FP16 forward/backward and all-reduce, FP32 master weights, dynamic loss scaling), gradient accumulation to reach about 400k-token batches, a doubled learning rate, and synchronous data-parallel SGD on up to 128 V100 GPUs with gradient communication overlapped with the backward pass. Training time to a fixed validation perplexity is the main measurement.

datasets.name: WMT'16 En-De
datasets.source: WMT'16, filtered version from Vaswani et al. 2017

datasets.name: WMT'14 En-Fr
datasets.source: WMT'14, setup of Gehring et al. 2017

datasets.name: Paracrawl
datasets.size: more than 4.5B pairs En-De, more than 4.2B En-Fr; filtered to 140M En-De and 129M En-Fr
datasets.split: mixed with WMT at sampling ratio 1:1 (En-De) or 3:1 WMT:Paracrawl (En-Fr)
datasets.preprocessing: drop pairs with source/target length ratio above 1.5, sentences over 250 words, and copies; En-De 4.6B to 700M; score with a model trained on WMT'14 news commentary and keep 140M pairs with best average token log-likelihood; WMT BPE vocabulary reused

models.name: Transformer big (fairseq-py, PyTorch)
models.architecture: encoder-decoder Transformer, ReLU feed-forward, post-layer-norm after residual

training.lr_schedule: linear warmup then inverse square root decay in the number of steps (Vaswani et al. 2017)
training.batch_size: 25k target tokens baseline; up to 402k tokens (cumul 16); 365k with 5k tokens/GPU and cumul 10; sub-batch at most 3.5k tokens per GPU (5k with FP16)
training.steps: 192k updates for the FP32 reference to perplexity 4.32; 9.5k-9.7k updates with the 402k batch (Table 1)
training.precision: FP16 forward/backward and all-reduce; FP32 master weights, loss and optimizer; dynamic loss scaling, raised if no overflow in 2,000 updates
training.regularisation: label smoothing 0.1; average of last 10 checkpoints for final results
training.hardware: DGX-1 nodes, 8 NVIDIA V100 GPUs each, Infiniband, NCCL2 and torch.distributed; up to 16 nodes (128 GPUs)
training.wall_clock: En-De 85 min and En-Fr 512 min on 16 nodes (Table 2); with Paracrawl 539 and 794 min (Table 3)
training.seeds: Table 1 times averaged over 3 random seeds

inference.decoding: beam search, beam width 4, length penalty 0.6

other.checkpoint_averaging: not used except where specified (last 10 for Tables 2 and 3)

metrics.name: training time to validation perplexity 4.32 (2.11 NLL)
metrics.definition: average time excluding validation and model saving, over 3 seeds, newstest13

eval.protocol: Speed measured to a fixed validation perplexity on newstest13; final BLEU on newstest14.

results.claim: Combined FP16, accumulation, 2x lr and larger per-GPU batches cut single-machine (8 V100) time to the same perplexity by 4.9x.
results.setup: Big Transformer, WMT En-De, 8 V100, newstest13, 3 seeds
results.quote: we reduce training time from 1, 429 min to 294 min to reach the same perplexity on the same hardware (8x NVIDIA V100), i.e. a 4.9x speedup.

results.claim: 16-bit training alone gives a 2.9x speedup with BLEU unchanged.
results.quote: shows that 16-bit results in a 2.9x speedup.

results.claim: Training on 16 nodes with overlap of communication and backward reaches the target perplexity in 32 minutes, a 44.7x speedup over the FP32 reference.
results.table: Table 1, row + overlap comm+bwd, columns time and speedup (32, 44.7x)

results.claim: Overlapping gradient communication with the backward pass saves 15% of 16-node time.
results.quote: we can further reduce training time by 15%, from 37 minutes to just 32 minutes

results.claim: New state of the art on WMT'14 En-De of 29.3 BLEU in 85 minutes on 128 GPUs.
results.setup: Big Transformer, WMT'16 En-De, 16 nodes, average of last 10 checkpoints, tokenized BLEU
results.quote: On WMT’14 En-De test set, we report 29.3 BLEU

results.claim: New state of the art on WMT'14 En-Fr of 43.2 BLEU in 8.5 hours on 128 GPUs.
results.setup: Big Transformer, WMT'14 En-Fr 36M pairs, 16 nodes
results.quote: We improve the state-of-the-art for WMT’14 En-Fr to 43.2 vs.

results.claim: Adding filtered Paracrawl raises En-De BLEU to 29.8 but lowers En-Fr to 42.1.
results.setup: WMT + 140M filtered Paracrawl pairs, sampling ratio 1:1, 16 nodes, 539 min
results.quote: We ﬁnd that Paracrawl improves BLEU on En–De to 29.8
results.table: Table 3, row WMT + Paracrawl, column En-De

results.claim: Accumulating gradients over 16 backward passes raises throughput by 36% in tokens per second and cuts time from 495 to 447 min.
results.quote: leading to a 36% increase in tokens/sec (Table 1, cumul)

results.claim: Large batches converge more slowly per epoch but faster per optimization step, so they parallelise.
results.setup: Transformer, batch sizes 25k, 100k, 200k, 400k target tokens, WMT En-De, newstest13
results.quote: Training with large batches is less data-efﬁcient, but can be parallelized.

results.claim: Sub-batch compute time varies widely (mean 0.11 s, slowest 0.228 s, fastest 0.049 s) over 44K sub-batches, creating stragglers.
results.setup: WMT En-De, sub-batches of at most 3.5k tokens
results.quote: the mean time to process a sub-batch is 0.11 seconds, the slowest sub-batch takes 0.228 seconds and the fastest 0.049 seconds

results.claim: Balancing sub-batches by estimated processing time lifts throughput from 143k to 150k tok/s and time from 495 to 479 min, less effective than gradient accumulation (447 min).
results.quote: reducing the training time to reach 4.32 perplexity from 495 to 479 minutes

results.claim: 16-node training is only about 10x faster than 1-node training.
results.quote: 16-node training is only ∼10x faster than 1-node training.

limits: Single architecture (big Transformer) and task (translation), WMT En-De and En-Fr only.
Multi-node scaling is sublinear: 16 nodes gives only about 10x over 1 node; authors leave better batching and communication to future work.
Paracrawl did not help En-Fr (42.1 vs 43.2 BLEU).
Naive shape-matched sub-batches fail to converge to the target perplexity.
Large-batch results depend on LR warmup and a 2x LR retuned by hand; no general batch-size/LR rule is given.
Hardware (V100, FP16 Tensor Cores) and BLEU state of the art have dated.
